name: Nebo-Sarsekim
title: Babylonian Official at the Fall of Jerusalem
summary: Nebo-Sarsekim was one of the Babylonian officials who participated in the siege and conquest of Jerusalem in 586 BC during the reign of King Nebuchadnezzar. He is mentioned in Jeremiah 39:3 among the Babylonian officers who took their positions at the Middle Gate after the city wall was breached. His existence is remarkably confirmed by a Babylonian cuneiform tablet in the British Museum, which strengthens the historical reliability of the biblical text.

keyEvents.title: The Siege of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Nebuchadnezzar's army besieged Jerusalem, and Nebo-Sarsekim was among the Babylonian officers who took part in this long siege.

keyEvents.title: Breaching of Jerusalem's Wall
keyEvents.description: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah's reign, the Babylonians broke through the city wall, and the city fell to the Babylonian army.

keyEvents.title: Babylonian Officials at the Middle Gate
keyEvents.description: Nebo-Sarsekim and other Babylonian officials took their position at the Middle Gate as a sign of victory and takeover of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: King Zedekiah's Flight and Capture
keyEvents.description: When Zedekiah saw the Babylonian officers at the gate, he fled during the night but was captured on the plains of Jericho and brought to Nebuchadnezzar.

keyEvents.title: The Destruction of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: After the conquest, the walls of Jerusalem were torn down and the city burned, just as the prophet Jeremiah had predicted as God's judgment against Judah.
